title: The greatest pearl
text: Kino, a poor pearl diver, lives in a brush hut by the sea with his wife, Juana, and their baby son, Coyotito. One peaceful dawn a scorpion stings Coyotito. The family carries him to the town doctor, but the doctor refuses to treat a poor native family who cannot pay.
While Juana tends the baby with a seaweed poultice and prays for luck, Kino dives for oysters and brings up a huge one. Inside lies the greatest pearl anyone has ever seen.

Before Kino is even home, the whole town knows. The priest, the shopkeepers, the beggars and the pearl buyers all begin to want something from the pearl. Kino tells his neighbours and his brother, Juan Tomás, what it will buy: a church wedding, new clothes, a rifle, and above all schooling for Coyotito. Suddenly the doctor comes to treat the baby after all, gives him a white powder that makes him violently ill, then “cures” him, and Kino suspects a trick.

As chapter 3 closes, someone has crept into the hut in the night to steal the pearl, and Kino has fought him off in the dark and been struck on the head. Juana begs him to throw the pearl back into the sea, saying it will destroy them, but Kino refuses: this is their one chance, and he means to fight for it.

title: Flight into the night
text: When a scorpion stung his baby son, Coyotito, the poor pearl diver Kino was turned away by the town doctor. Then Kino found the greatest pearl anyone had ever seen, and dreamed of a church wedding with his wife, Juana, a rifle and schooling for his son. But the pearl set the whole town against him. The doctor suddenly came to “treat” the baby, and that night an intruder tried to steal the pearl.

Kino took the pearl to the buyers, who pretended to compete but each offered only a fraction of its worth. Sensing a trap, he refused and vowed to sell it in the capital, despite his brother Juan Tomás’s warning that men who tried that were never heard from again. That night he was attacked once more.

In the dark, Juana tried to throw the pearl into the sea, and Kino caught her and beat her. On the way back he was attacked again and killed a man. Then the family found their canoe smashed and their hut in flames. They hid all day in Juan Tomás’s house, while the neighbours thought them dead, and Kino told his brother that the pearl has become his soul.
As chapter 5 closes, darkness has fallen, and Kino, Juana and Coyotito have set out on foot, heading north toward the capital with the pearl.
